paragraphs.title: The Command to Go Up to the Land

easy.question: To whom did the Lord speak in these verses?
answers: Moses
Aaron
Joshua
easy.explanation: The first verse says explicitly, “And the Lord said unto Moses.”

easy.question: To which land were Moses and the people commanded to go?
answers: The land of Egypt
The land the Lord swore to give to the patriarchs
The land of the Philistines
easy.explanation: The Lord commanded them to go to the land He promised to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

easy.question: What did the Lord promise to send before the people?
answers: A prophet
An army
An angel
easy.explanation: Verse 2 says, “And I will send an angel before thee.”

medium.question: What would the angel sent before the people do?
answers: Drive out the peoples of Canaan
Build houses for them
Return them to Egypt
medium.explanation: The Lord said that the angel would go before them and drive the peoples of Canaan out of the land.

medium.question: Why did the Lord say that He would not go up in the midst of the people?
answers: Because the people did not know the way
Because they were stiff-necked and might be consumed along the way
Because the land was too far away
medium.explanation: Because the people were stiff-necked, the Lord said, “lest I consume thee in the way.”

medium.question: What does “stiff-necked” mean in the statement “thou art a stiffnecked people”?
answers: A stubborn people unwilling to change its ways
A physically strong people
A people that does not know the way
medium.explanation: In this warning, “stiff-necked” means stubborn and unwilling to change or listen.

challenge.question: What can we infer from the Lord’s mention of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob?
answers: The land was a new gift never promised before
Going to the land was connected to the promise given to the patriarchs
The patriarchs would now lead the people
challenge.explanation: The Lord presents the land as a continuation of the oath given to the patriarchs and their descendants.

challenge.question: What cause-and-effect relationship appears in verse 3?
answers: Because the people are stiff-necked, the Lord fears consuming them on the way
Because the land is good, the people remain in Egypt
Because the angel is sent, the people do not need to travel
challenge.explanation: The verse connects the people’s stubborn character with the danger that the Lord might consume them during the journey.

challenge.question: What special detail is given in the description of the land in verse 3?
answers: It is described as a land of high mountains
It is described as a land surrounded by water
It is described as a land flowing with milk and honey
challenge.explanation: The phrase “a land flowing with milk and honey” emphasizes the land’s abundance and goodness.

questions.question: What can we infer from the Lord’s mention of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob?
answers: The land was a new gift never promised before
Going to the land was connected to the promise given to the patriarchs
The patriarchs would now lead the people
questions.explanation: The Lord presents the land as a continuation of the oath given to the patriarchs and their descendants.

questions.question: What cause-and-effect relationship appears in verse 3?
answers: Because the people are stiff-necked, the Lord fears consuming them on the way
Because the land is good, the people remain in Egypt
Because the angel is sent, the people do not need to travel
questions.explanation: The verse connects the people’s stubborn character with the danger that the Lord might consume them during the journey.

questions.question: What special detail is given in the description of the land in verse 3?
answers: It is described as a land of high mountains
It is described as a land surrounded by water
It is described as a land flowing with milk and honey
questions.explanation: The phrase “a land flowing with milk and honey” emphasizes the land’s abundance and goodness.

paragraphs.title: The People Mourn and Remove Their Ornaments

easy.question: What did the Israelites do when they heard the evil tidings?
answers: They mourned
They danced
They went to war
easy.explanation: The verse says that they mourned, meaning that the Israelites grieved.

easy.question: What did the Israelites not put on themselves?
answers: Clothing
Ornaments and jewelry
Shoes
easy.explanation: The text says that no one put his ornaments on himself.

easy.question: Where did the Israelites remove their ornaments?
answers: In Egypt
In Jerusalem
By Mount Horeb
easy.explanation: The final verse says that they removed their ornaments by Mount Horeb.

medium.question: Why were the Israelites told to remove their ornaments?
answers: So that the Lord could decide what to do with them
So they could begin a festive journey
So they could enrich the tabernacle
medium.explanation: The Lord told them to remove their ornaments so that He might know what to do with them.

medium.question: In the phrase “no man did put on him his ornaments,” what does “ornaments” mean?
answers: Foods
Jewelry and decorations
Books
medium.explanation: The context says they did not put them on themselves, and the passage later says to remove them; the word refers to jewelry and decorations.

medium.question: What is the correct order of events according to the verses?
answers: The people removed their ornaments, heard the news, and then mourned
The people left Mount Horeb, heard the news, and then put on ornaments
The people heard the evil tidings, mourned, and did not put on their ornaments
medium.explanation: First the people heard the evil tidings and mourned; afterward, the text says they did not put on their ornaments.

challenge.question: What does “stiff-necked people” mean in this context?
answers: A stubborn people that does not easily change its ways
A people that does not wear clothing
A people living in a mountainous area
challenge.explanation: “Stiff-necked” describes a person or people who are stubborn and do not easily submit or change their ways.

challenge.question: What can we understand from the Israelites removing their ornaments after hearing the evil tidings?
answers: They were preparing for a celebration
They were expressing mourning and submission before the Lord
They wanted to change their clothing
challenge.explanation: Removing jewelry after hearing bad news expresses mourning and also responded to the Lord’s command.

challenge.question: What does the phrase “by Mount Horeb” teach about where the ornaments were removed?
answers: It happened in Egypt
The ornaments were removed only after entering the land
They removed them in the area of Mount Horeb
challenge.explanation: The verse states that the Israelites removed their ornaments by Mount Horeb, either there or from that point onward.

questions.question: What does “stiff-necked people” mean in this context?
answers: A stubborn people that does not easily change its ways
A people that does not wear clothing
A people living in a mountainous area
questions.explanation: “Stiff-necked” describes a person or people who are stubborn and do not easily submit or change their ways.

questions.question: What can we understand from the Israelites removing their ornaments after hearing the evil tidings?
answers: They were preparing for a celebration
They were expressing mourning and submission before the Lord
They wanted to change their clothing
questions.explanation: Removing jewelry after hearing bad news expresses mourning and also responded to the Lord’s command.

questions.question: What does the phrase “by Mount Horeb” teach about where the ornaments were removed?
answers: It happened in Egypt
The ornaments were removed only after entering the land
They removed them in the area of Mount Horeb
questions.explanation: The verse states that the Israelites removed their ornaments by Mount Horeb, either there or from that point onward.

easy.question: Where did Moses set up the Tabernacle?
answers: Outside the camp, far from it
In the center of the camp
On Mount Sinai
easy.explanation: Moses pitched the Tabernacle outside the camp, far from it.

easy.question: What did the people do when Moses went out to the Tabernacle?
answers: They entered their tents
They rose, stood at their tent doors, and watched him
They left the camp
easy.explanation: The people rose, stood at their tent doors, and watched Moses until he entered the Tabernacle.

easy.question: Who remained inside the Tabernacle and did not leave it?
answers: Joshua son of Nun
All the people
Aaron
easy.explanation: Joshua son of Nun, Moses’ servant, did not depart from the Tabernacle.

medium.question: What happened after Moses entered the Tabernacle?
answers: The cloudy pillar descended and stood at the door
All the people entered the camp
Joshua left the Tabernacle
medium.explanation: When Moses entered the Tabernacle, the cloudy pillar descended and stood at its door.

medium.question: Why did everyone who sought the Lord go out to the Tabernacle?
answers: To see Joshua
To seek the Lord at the special place
To get away from Moses
medium.explanation: The verse says that everyone who sought the Lord went out to the Tabernacle outside the camp.

medium.question: In the phrase “departed not out of the tabernacle,” what does “departed not” mean?
answers: Did not move or leave
Did not speak
Did not see
medium.explanation: The phrase means that Joshua did not move away or leave; he remained inside the Tabernacle.

challenge.question: What does “face to face” mean in the description of the Lord speaking with Moses?
answers: Moses literally saw the Lord’s face
The communication was direct and close, like a person speaking with a friend
The conversation took place only before all the people
challenge.explanation: The verse compares it to a man speaking with his friend, so it refers to direct and close communication.

challenge.question: What did the people do after seeing the cloudy pillar standing at the Tabernacle door?
answers: They worshiped, each person at his tent door
They all entered the Tabernacle
They hid inside the camp
challenge.explanation: When they saw the cloudy pillar, all the people rose and worshiped, each at his tent door.

challenge.question: What difference between Moses and Joshua is described at the end of the passage?
answers: Moses stayed in the Tabernacle and Joshua returned to the camp
They both remained in the Tabernacle the whole time
Moses returned to the camp, while Joshua remained in the Tabernacle
challenge.explanation: The verse says that Moses returned to the camp, while Joshua did not depart from the Tabernacle.

questions.question: What does “face to face” mean in the description of the Lord speaking with Moses?
answers: Moses literally saw the Lord’s face
The communication was direct and close, like a person speaking with a friend
The conversation took place only before all the people
questions.explanation: The verse compares it to a man speaking with his friend, so it refers to direct and close communication.

questions.question: What did the people do after seeing the cloudy pillar standing at the Tabernacle door?
answers: They worshiped, each person at his tent door
They all entered the Tabernacle
They hid inside the camp
questions.explanation: When they saw the cloudy pillar, all the people rose and worshiped, each at his tent door.

questions.question: What difference between Moses and Joshua is described at the end of the passage?
answers: Moses stayed in the Tabernacle and Joshua returned to the camp
They both remained in the Tabernacle the whole time
Moses returned to the camp, while Joshua remained in the Tabernacle
questions.explanation: The verse says that Moses returned to the camp, while Joshua did not depart from the Tabernacle.

easy.question: Who said, “My presence shall go with thee”?
answers: The Lord
Moses
The people
easy.explanation: The Lord said to Moses, “My presence shall go with thee.”

easy.question: What did Moses ask if the Lord would not go with the people?
answers: That He give them a king
That He not bring them up from that place
That He return to Egypt
easy.explanation: Moses said, “If thy presence go not with me, carry us not up hence.”

easy.question: To whom did the Lord say, “Thou hast found grace in my sight, and I know thee by name”?
answers: The people of Israel
Aaron
Moses
easy.explanation: The Lord said these words to Moses.

medium.question: What does “we shall be separated” mean in the statement “we shall be separated, I and thy people, from all the people”?
answers: We will be distinguished and special
We will fall to the ground
We will fear the nations
medium.explanation: The context shows that Moses asks for the people to be distinguished and special because the Lord goes with them.

medium.question: According to Moses, how would it be known that he and the people had found grace in the Lord’s sight?
answers: If they received a large land
If the Lord went with them
If they defeated every nation
medium.explanation: Moses says the sign of their acceptance would be that the Lord went with them.

medium.question: What is the correct order of events in the passage?
answers: Moses asks not to go up, then the Lord promises to go, and finally Moses asks to know the way
The Lord promises to go, then says Moses has found grace, and finally Moses asks not to go up
Moses asks to know the Lord’s way, the Lord promises to go, and then Moses stresses that they must not go up without His presence
medium.explanation: First Moses asks to know the Lord’s way; then the Lord promises that His presence will go; finally Moses makes their journey conditional on that presence.

challenge.question: What can we infer from Moses’ request, “Carry us not up hence”?
answers: The divine presence mattered more to him than progress itself
He never wanted to reach the land
He wanted to remain alone in the wilderness
challenge.explanation: Moses was willing not to advance if the Lord would not go with the people, showing that the Lord’s presence was essential to him.

challenge.question: What does the phrase “I and thy people” emphasize in verse 16?
answers: Only Moses would have a special relationship with the Lord
The Lord’s special relationship included Moses and all the people
The people were unrelated to Moses’ request
challenge.explanation: Moses emphasizes that the Lord’s guidance would distinguish both him and the people from all other nations.

challenge.question: What does “my presence” mean in the statement “My presence shall go with thee”?
answers: The Lord’s physical face
The direction in which Moses would go
The Lord’s presence and guidance
challenge.explanation: The context shows that “my presence” refers to the Lord being with and guiding the people, not to a physical face.

questions.question: What can we infer from Moses’ request, “Carry us not up hence”?
answers: The divine presence mattered more to him than progress itself
He never wanted to reach the land
He wanted to remain alone in the wilderness
questions.explanation: Moses was willing not to advance if the Lord would not go with the people, showing that the Lord’s presence was essential to him.

answers: Only Moses would have a special relationship with the Lord
The Lord’s special relationship included Moses and all the people
The people were unrelated to Moses’ request
questions.explanation: Moses emphasizes that the Lord’s guidance would distinguish both him and the people from all other nations.

questions.question: What does “my presence” mean in the statement “My presence shall go with thee”?
answers: The Lord’s physical face
The direction in which Moses would go
The Lord’s presence and guidance
questions.explanation: The context shows that “my presence” refers to the Lord being with and guiding the people, not to a physical face.

paragraphs.title: Moses Asks to See the Lord’s Glory

easy.question: What did Moses ask to see?
answers: The Lord’s glory
The land of Israel
The tablets
easy.explanation: Moses asked the Lord, “I beseech thee, shew me thy glory.”

easy.question: What was said about a person who cannot see the Lord’s face?
answers: He would fall asleep
He could not remain alive
He would become a king
easy.explanation: The verse says, “There shall no man see me, and live.”

easy.question: What did the Lord say He would make pass before Moses?
answers: His people
His angels
All His goodness
easy.explanation: The Lord said, “I will make all my goodness pass before thee.”

medium.question: What is the correct order of events in the verses?
answers: Moses asks to see the Lord’s glory, and the Lord answers that He will show His goodness but not His face
The Lord refuses to speak with Moses, and Moses leaves
Moses sees the Lord’s face and then asks for His glory
medium.explanation: First Moses asks to see the Lord’s glory; then the Lord promises to show His goodness and explains that His face cannot be seen.

medium.question: In the phrase “I will be gracious to whom I will be gracious,” what does “be gracious” mean?
answers: Punish whoever He chooses
Grant favor and goodness to whoever He chooses
Hide whoever He chooses
medium.explanation: The phrase concerns grace and favor; the context shows that the Lord decides to whom He will grant goodness and mercy.

medium.question: Why did the Lord not grant Moses’ request to see His face directly?
answers: Because Moses did not ask strongly enough
Because the Lord did not hear him
Because a person cannot see the Lord’s face and live
medium.explanation: The Lord explicitly explained, “There shall no man see me, and live.”

challenge.question: What is the main difference between what Moses asked to see and what the Lord promised to show him?
answers: Moses asked to see the Lord’s glory, while the Lord promised to make His goodness pass before him without allowing a full view of His face
Moses asked to see the people, and the Lord showed him His face
Moses asked to see the future, and the Lord showed him Egypt
challenge.explanation: Moses asked to see the Lord’s glory, but the answer distinguishes between the passing of His goodness and seeing His face, which is impossible for a human being.

challenge.question: What can we infer from the words “Thou canst not see my face”?
answers: Moses was not allowed to speak with the Lord at all
There is a limit to the human ability to perceive the Lord’s revelation
The Lord was unwilling to do anything for Moses
challenge.explanation: The verse does not rule out communication between Moses and the Lord; it sets a limit on humanity’s ability to see the Lord’s face.

challenge.question: Who proclaims the Lord’s name in the phrase “I will proclaim the name of the Lord before thee”?
answers: Moses proclaims the Lord’s name before the people
The people proclaim the Lord’s name before Moses
The Lord proclaims His own name before Moses
challenge.explanation: The Lord is speaking, so the statement means that He will proclaim the Lord’s name before Moses as part of the revelation given to him.

questions.question: What is the main difference between what Moses asked to see and what the Lord promised to show him?
answers: Moses asked to see the Lord’s glory, while the Lord promised to make His goodness pass before him without allowing a full view of His face
Moses asked to see the people, and the Lord showed him His face
Moses asked to see the future, and the Lord showed him Egypt
questions.explanation: Moses asked to see the Lord’s glory, but the answer distinguishes between the passing of His goodness and seeing His face, which is impossible for a human being.

questions.question: What can we infer from the words “Thou canst not see my face”?
answers: Moses was not allowed to speak with the Lord at all
There is a limit to the human ability to perceive the Lord’s revelation
The Lord was unwilling to do anything for Moses
questions.explanation: The verse does not rule out communication between Moses and the Lord; it sets a limit on humanity’s ability to see the Lord’s face.

questions.question: Who proclaims the Lord’s name in the phrase “I will proclaim the name of the Lord before thee”?
answers: Moses proclaims the Lord’s name before the people
The people proclaim the Lord’s name before Moses
The Lord proclaims His own name before Moses
questions.explanation: The Lord is speaking, so the statement means that He will proclaim the Lord’s name before Moses as part of the revelation given to him.

paragraphs.title: In the Cleft of the Rock Under the Lord’s Hand

easy.question: On what did the Lord command Moses to stand?
answers: The rock
The river
The mountain
easy.explanation: The Lord said to Moses, “Thou shalt stand upon a rock.”

easy.question: Where would the Lord put Moses?
answers: In the cloud
In a cleft of the rock
In the Tabernacle
easy.explanation: The Lord promised to put Moses in a cleft of the rock.

easy.question: What would Moses not see?
answers: The Lord’s glory
The rock
The Lord’s face
easy.explanation: At the end of the passage, the Lord says, “My face shall not be seen.”

medium.question: Why would the Lord cover Moses with His hand?
answers: To protect him until the Lord had passed by
To hide the rock
To move Moses away from the place
medium.explanation: The Lord would cover Moses with His hand while He passed by so that Moses would not see His face.

medium.question: In the phrase “I will put thee in a cleft of the rock,” what is a “cleft”?
answers: The top of the rock
A crack or hollow in the rock
The color of the rock
medium.explanation: The context shows that Moses would be placed in a protected opening in the rock; a cleft is a crack or hollow.

medium.question: What is the correct order of events?
answers: Moses sees the Lord’s face and then enters the rock
The Lord removes His hand and then covers Moses
Moses stands on the rock, enters the cleft, and afterward sees the Lord’s back parts
medium.explanation: First Moses is told to stand on the rock; then the Lord places him in the cleft; afterward Moses sees the Lord’s back parts.

challenge.question: Which detail shows that Moses’ view was limited rather than complete?
answers: He saw only the Lord’s back parts and not His face
He did not see the rock
He saw only Moses’ hand
challenge.explanation: The verse emphasizes that Moses would see the Lord’s back parts, but His face would not be seen.

challenge.question: When does the Lord remove His hand from Moses?
answers: Before Moses stands on the rock
After the Lord has passed by
Before the Lord puts Moses in the cleft
challenge.explanation: The Lord says He will cover Moses “while I pass by,” and only afterward remove His hand.

challenge.question: What can we infer from the sequence “while my glory passeth by” and “while I pass by”?
answers: The glory and the Lord pass by before the hand is removed
Moses passes before the Lord’s glory
The glory remains in the rock and does not pass by
challenge.explanation: The passage describes the Lord’s glory and the Lord passing by while Moses is protected by the hand; only afterward can he see the Lord’s back parts.

questions.question: Which detail shows that Moses’ view was limited rather than complete?
answers: He saw only the Lord’s back parts and not His face
He did not see the rock
He saw only Moses’ hand
questions.explanation: The verse emphasizes that Moses would see the Lord’s back parts, but His face would not be seen.

questions.question: When does the Lord remove His hand from Moses?
answers: Before Moses stands on the rock
After the Lord has passed by
Before the Lord puts Moses in the cleft
questions.explanation: The Lord says He will cover Moses “while I pass by,” and only afterward remove His hand.

questions.question: What can we infer from the sequence “while my glory passeth by” and “while I pass by”?
answers: The glory and the Lord pass by before the hand is removed
Moses passes before the Lord’s glory
The glory remains in the rock and does not pass by
questions.explanation: The passage describes the Lord’s glory and the Lord passing by while Moses is protected by the hand; only afterward can he see the Lord’s back parts.
